from.place: Proof, second paragraph: "finite-type field algebras are excellent"; the J-2 condition for the ground field in the field-excellence input. Supporting a regular sequence at a prime spreads to a principal neighbourhood.

title: A regular sequence at a prime spreads to a principal neighbourhood
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal, and let $r\ge0$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in R$. If their images form a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], then there exists $g\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that their images form a regular sequence in the principal localization $R[1/g]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].
